messages.subject: Connecting to MySql with SSH tunneling
messages.subject_clean: Connecting to MySql with SSH tunneling
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to connect to a remote MySql databse through SSH tunneling. I could succesfully connect to DB

1. by using "username" and "password".
2. by using username and local private key
3. by using username, local private key and key phrase.

I am facing an issue when I am trying to do ssh tunnelling with username and private key which is on remote machine.(say for example private key file present on ftp or s3 etc.) Is there a way to do ssh tunnelling with remote private key?

Please help me with your suggestions.

Thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Can shinyapps.io use cached rmarkdown files
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Can shinyapps.io use cached rmarkdown files
messages.body_plain:
On 2017-08-30 at 17:40, Tareef Kawaf <tar...@rstudio.com> wrote:
>

> I am not aware of a way to do that.  Essentially, you are looking to avoid running the chunks on the server, is that right?

Exactly.

> I wonder if you could refactor your code such that you write out the RDS/RDA or feather files and upload those instead.  If that would work, you would obviously need to have a separate script that created the RDAs or RDS or feather files so that your R Markdown code is just a consumer.

This is exactly what caching does so I hoped to avoid the trouble of writing it explicitly myself. Also, it allows to keep all the code related to this project in the same rmarkdown file rather than having the rmarkdown simply be a visualisation of data that is pre-processed. It is easier to maintain this way.

I actually have a shiny-server running and if I upload the .Rmd file and all the associated folders with the .RData caches, pre-rendered images etc. it just works as I intend it too. It just does not work on shinyapps.io...

JO Irisson

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Protocol sftp not supported or disabled in libcurl
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Protocol sftp not supported or disabled in libcurl
messages.body_plain:
Correct, users are not directly privileged to install system packages, they are installed as a side effect of installing R packages via shinyapps-package-dependencies <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies>
Unlikely we would switch our Linux distribution.

You might be better off self-hosting in this case.

>

>
> I wonder how this Ubuntu issue could be resolved or circumvented? What about other linux distributions? Any other ideas or suggestions you have would be great.
>

messages.subject: Creation of plot using Action Button in R Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Creation of plot using Action Button in R Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi, the following R script creates a shiny dashboard page with two buttons and one plot section.
The second button "Processing" works fine but the first button "Resource" creates the process_map()
plot outside the shiny page in the output pane. I want a functionality where when I click on button "Resource",
it gives me the filter menu using "ifilter_resource",post that I should select the resources to be filtered,
and change happens to the process_map that I have built within the shiny page. Please help and big thanks.

## app.R ##
library(bupaR)
library(edeaR)
library(eventdataR)
library(processmapR)
library(processmonitR)
library(xesreadR)
library(petrinetR)

ui <- dashboardPage(
dashboardHeader(title = "Business Process Mining"),

dashboardSidebar(
width = 0,
conditionalPanel(condition = "input.tabselected == 1")
),
dashboardBody(

# Creation of tabs and tabsetPanel
tabsetPanel(type = "tab",
            tabPanel("Overview", value = 1,

                     fluidRow(
                       column(1,
                              tags$br(actionButton("buttonprocmapone",
"Resource")),
                              tags$br(),
                              tags$br(actionButton("buttonprocmaptwo",
"Processing"))
                       ),
                       tags$br(),

                       column(10,

                              plotOutput("proc_map_plot")
                       ))

            ))))
server <- function(input, output) {

#Code for Resource Dashboard Resource Involvement Plots

proc_map <- reactiveValues(proc_map_one = 0, proc_map_two = 0)

observeEvent(input$buttonprocmapone, {
proc_map$proc_map_one <- 1
proc_map$proc_map_two <- 0

})

observeEvent(input$buttonprocmaptwo, {
proc_map$proc_map_one <- 0
proc_map$proc_map_two <- 1

})

output$proc_map_plot <- renderPlot(
{
  if(proc_map$proc_map_one)
    pt1 = ifilter_resource(patients)
    pt1 %>% process_map()
  else
    if(proc_map$proc_map_two)
      patients %>%resource_involvement("resource") %>% plot
  else
    return()
}

)
}
shinyApp(ui, server)

Hello,

I have tried to use my own development-release packages. They are hosted on Bitbucket (private repo) in Shinyapps. The deployment of the app failed. It was no suprise as Shiny docs (http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/getting-started.html#using-your-r-packages-in-the-cloud) explain that only Gihub and BioConductor services are supported yet.

In my case, migrating to Github would be both complex and costly.
Does the Shinyapp team plan to support Bitbucket repos in Shinyapps ?

Do you know some workarounds ? Maybe using the devtools::install ?
Thanks a lot !

Julien

messages.subject_clean: Using user written packages hosted by Bitbucket in Shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
BitBucket is not currently supported, and while it is on our backlog, it has not been scheduled.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny API Deployment issue

shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> does not currently support listening on arbitrary ports and having internet traffic routed to it, so I don't believe a plumber application will function in the way one would want.

Jason

Your Shiny application cannot contain install commands. It should only contain library references.

Remove the devtools::install_github("nstrayer/shinyswipr"), but leave the library(shinyswipr)

You are also correct, you cannot call setwd with an absolute path. The filesystem on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is not the same as your local computer. All files should be contained in the project directory and can be referenced with relative paths.

Once you have made those changes, if you are still having issues, please send new error output.

messages.subject: Re: Authentication for multiple apps
messages.subject_clean: Authentication for multiple apps
messages.body_plain:
Thanks! I had only used the magic of the push-button deploy interface and the application authentication dashboard on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> as described at https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html.

So with addAuthorizedUser() and the related rsconnect functions, I gather that I can do the authentication setup from my local machine without using the dashboard interface on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. Given that I will have lot's of IDs and lots of apps to manage, I will write a little package to manage this and let R on my local machine handle the tedious and intricate task of connecting each user ID to the applications to be authorized for that user. I guess I should have realized that the push-button deploy interface would be written in terms of rsconnect functions and that I can call these directly.

On Wednesday, September 20, 2017 at 10:37:54 AM UTC-4, Joshua Spiewak wrote:
> You may want to look at rsconnect::addAuthorizedUser to programmatically manage access.
>
> On Tuesday, September 19, 2017 at 5:06:40 PM UTC-4, Daniel Kaplan wrote:
> > I'm putting together multiple learnr tutorials deployed on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. I need to be able to control access to the whole set of apps on a user-by-user basis.
> >
> > I see how, in the standard plan, I can authorize a user to access a tutorial. But I'll have dozens of related related tutorials. It would be impractical to manage the users for each tutorial independently. Instead, I'd like to be able in one operation to authorize/de-authorize a user for a whole set of tutorials.

Hi all,

I have a private app at https://proxe.shinyapps.io/PRoXe/ that is disconnecting from server after minimal use (switching tabPanel, filtering a DT dataframe factor variable, have not exhausted this search). It runs just fine locally. My old version at a different URL works just fine at shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

I recently switched R versions (to 3.4.1) and updated all packages, including installing shiny, rsconnect, and DT from github. I can go roll these back one at a time.

Any thoughts? Is this a widespread issue, possibly?

Apologies for mentioning this in several comments and then also posting it here.

Thanks much,
Scott

It appears you might be using xlsx which is known to trigger this issue.

Hope that helps!

messages.body_plain:
In your project directory, there is a sub-directory "rsconnect/shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>" that then contains a directory with your account name, which contains a DCF file with the application name.

This file stores the application id of the application. If you delete the application via the dashboard, you need to remove this file so that a new application will be created with a new id.

>
> Preparing to deploy application...
>
> Error: HTTP 404
> GET https://api.shinyapps.io/v1/applications/217483
> Not Found
>
>
> I think it might try to update the older version but fails to find it, because it no longer exists. Any help on how to resolve this?

I have an app (richarddmorey.shinyapps.io/test/download.Rmd <http://richarddmorey.shinyapps.io/test/download.Rmd>) that, under some conditions, produces an error (using "stop()") to restrict people from seeing certain content. When run locally, the error is printed to the app:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-qlX_N28rt4U/WcoxkSMYarI/AAAAAAAAKYw/2KdEXmm-2MYRVNvuxWxfD-e8TtG2Uvs9gCLcBGAs/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2017-09-26%2Bat%2B11.49.12.png>

When I run this app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, the error is not reported, but instead I get a generic error:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-pitQV25nSxI/Wcox0AUBjkI/AAAAAAAAKY0/xrpjQkbvJPQVra8YzwZ5gG1C0cmjK50sACLcBGAs/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2017-09-26%2Bat%2B11.49.57.png>

The logs show the error, as expected:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-JyyL85eB1Es/Wcox6zbopyI/AAAAAAAAKY4/aflGCNXu8qc2yH5gjWSMJf6EZSovnM2QwCLcBGAs/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2017-09-26%2Bat%2B11.50.10.png>

But this is confusing to users. Is there a way to get shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> to report the error back to the user, instead of the "Check logs" error message?

Thanks,
Richard

messages.body_plain:
Update 12/1/2017: 54.204.29.251 has been released. This post will remain pinned until 1/1/2018 as a reminder.

In order for applications running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> to access protected resources, we have documented <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html#firewalls> the IP addresses that are required to be whitelisted.

Previously there was a fourth IP address that we no longer have in active use. We plan to release this IP address on 12/1/2017, at which time it may be used by unrelated services that we do not manage or control.

If you have whitelisted 54.204.29.251, please be sure to remove it from your firewall rules prior to 12/1/2017.
